1	# HTTP Request Node — Planning
2	
3	> **MUST READ FIRST — confirm Managed HTTP Request fits your use case before authoring:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md). This planning doc is the flow-specific layer on top of it.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests — both connector-authenticated and manual. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated and does not pass IS credentials at runtime.
10	
11	## When to Use a Managed HTTP Request Node
12	
13	| Situation | Use Managed HTTP? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Connector exists but lacks the specific curated activity | Yes — connector mode ([impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md)), **if the connector supports HTTP request activity** (verify `HasHttpRequest` — see [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)) |
16	| No connector exists, but service has a REST API | Yes — manual mode ([impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md)) |
17	| Quick prototyping against any REST API | Yes — manual mode ([impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md)) |
18	| Connector exists and covers the use case | No — use [Connector Activity](../connector/planning.md) |
19	| Target system has no API (desktop app) | No — use [RPA Workflow](../rpa/planning.md) |
20	
21	For the two-mode concept (connector vs. manual) and the `url` / auth rules per mode, see the platform doc linked at the top.
22	
23	## Ports
24	
25	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| `input` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic, one per `inputs.branches` entry) |
28	
29	- `default` — primary success output, or fallback when configured branches don't match.
30	- `error` — implicit error port; fires when the call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Shared with all action nodes — see [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
31	- `branch-{id}` — HTTP-specific, configured via `inputs.branches` (response-content routing). See [Conditional Branches](#conditional-branches) below.
32	
33	## Output Variables
34	
35	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — `{ body, code, method, rawStringBody, request }` on success
36	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — `{ code, message, detail, category, status }` when the error port fires
37	
38	## Conditional Branches
39	
40	Use `inputs.branches` when you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., empty vs non-empty results). For generic call-failure handling, prefer the shared `error` port instead — don't enumerate every bad status code as a branch.
41	
42	Each branch's `conditionExpression` is a JS expression with `$self` bound to the current HTTP node's output:
43	
44	```json
45	{
46	  "inputs": {
47	    "branches": [
48	      { "id": "hasItems",  "name": "Has Items",  "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
49	      { "id": "empty",     "name": "Empty",      "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
50	    ]
51	  }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	Wire `branch-hasItems` / `branch-empty` as source ports on outgoing edges. `default` fires when no branch condition matches.
56	
57	> **Do not use `=js:` on `conditionExpression`** — HTTP branch conditions are evaluated as JS automatically (same rule as decision/switch expressions). See [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#http-branch-condition-inputsbranchesconditionexpression).
58	
59	## Dynamic values
60	
61	IS activity input fields (`url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` under `bodyParameters`) do **not** resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — the template runner only applies to native flow fields. Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value; template literals with `${...}` interpolation or string concatenation both work. See [Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query) for the full rationale and examples.
62	
63	## Key Inputs (`--detail` for `node configure`)
64	
65	Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with a `--detail` JSON. The CLI builds the full `inputs.detail` payload, `bindings_v2.json`, and connection resource files automatically. **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`.**
66	
67	**Connector mode** (IS connection auth):
68	
69	| `--detail` Key | Required | Description |
70	| --- | --- | --- |
71	| `authentication` | Yes | `"connector"` |
72	| `method` | Yes | HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE |
73	| `targetConnector` | Yes | Target connector key (e.g., `"uipath-salesforce-slack"`) |
74	| `connectionId` | Yes | Target connector's IS connection ID (from `uip is connections list --all-folders`) |
75	| `folderKey` | Yes | Orchestrator folder key (from `uip is connections list --all-folders`) |
76	| `url` | No | API endpoint URL/path (e.g., `"/conversations.replies"`). Auto-fills both `bodyParameters.path` and `bodyParameters.url`. |
77	| `query` | No | Query parameters as key-value object |
78	| `headers` | No | Additional headers as key-value object |
79	| `body` | No | Request body (for POST/PUT/PATCH). Connector mode is **`application/json` only** (request and response) — no other content type. |
80	
81	**Manual mode** (no connector auth):
82	
83	| `--detail` Key | Required | Description |
84	| --- | --- | --- |
85	| `authentication` | Yes | `"manual"` |
86	| `method` | Yes | HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE |
87	| `url` | Yes | Full target URL |
88	| `query` | No | Query parameters as key-value object |
89	| `headers` | No | Additional headers as key-value object |
90	| `body` | No | Request body (for POST/PUT/PATCH) |
91	
92	## Prerequisites
93	
94	- `uip login` required (for both modes — node type comes from registry)
95	- For connector mode: connector must support the HTTP request activity — verify the `HasHttpRequest` flag via `uip is connectors get "<connector-key>"`. If false, fall back to manual mode — confirm the switch with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
96	- For connector mode: a healthy IS connection must exist for the **target connector**. If none exists, auto-fall-through to manual mode is the recommended fallback — but confirm the mode switch with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md Step 2 — HTTP-specific recovery](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection) for the user-confirmation flow (switch-to-manual / create-now / skip).
97	- `uip maestro flow registry pull` to cache the `core.action.http.v2` definition
98	
99	## Planning Annotation
100	
101	In the architectural plan, annotate managed HTTP nodes as:
102	- Connector mode: `managed-http: <service> — <operation>` (e.g., "managed-http: Slack — GET /conversations.replies")
103	- Manual mode: `managed-http: manual — <method> <url>` (e.g., "managed-http: manual — GET https://api.example.com/data")
104

1	# Flow Editing Operations — CLI Carve-Outs
2	
3	This is **not** a structural editing guide. Use direct `.flow` authoring via [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) for OOTB node/edge/variable CRUD, trigger swaps, output mapping, subflows, inline-agent node/wiring, non-connector resources, and in-place updates.
4	
5	> **When to use this file:** only for CLI-managed carve-outs documented by a plugin: connector activities, connector triggers, and managed HTTP nodes (both `node add` and `node configure`). If you landed here while adding/removing/wiring OOTB nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, or other structural graph elements, go back to the Edit / Write guide.
6	
7	The primitive commands below are support commands for carve-out workflows only. They are not an opt-in path for non-carve-out structural edits.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Primitive Commands for Carve-Out Workflows
12	
13	### Add a node
14	
15	```bash
16	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <node-type> --output json \
17	  --input '<INPUT_JSON>' \
18	  --label "<LABEL>" \
19	  --position <X>,<Y> \
20	  --parent <PARENT_NODE_ID>
21	```
22	
23	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
24	- Inserts node into `nodes` array with a generated `id`
25	- Copies the definition from the local registry cache into `definitions` (one per unique type)
26	- Adds node output variables to `variables.nodes`
27	
28	**Flags:**
29	
30	| Flag | Required | Description |
31	|------|----------|-------------|
32	| `--input` | No | JSON object of node-specific inputs (expression, script, URL, etc.). Omit for nodes with no inputs (merge, end, terminate). |
33	| `--label` | No | Display label shown on the canvas |
34	| `--position` | No | `x,y` coordinates. Any value is fine (e.g. `0,0`) — `flow format` rewrites positions on save. |
35	| `--parent` | No | ID of an existing container node (e.g. a `core.logic.loop`). Sets `parentId` on the new node, placing it inside that container. Required for every node in a loop body — see [loop/impl.md](plugins/loop/impl.md). |
36	| `--output json` | Yes (for parsing) | Structured JSON response with the assigned node `id` |
37	
38	**Shell quoting tip:** If `--input` JSON contains special characters (quotes, braces, `$vars`), write it to a temp file and pass `--input "$(cat /tmp/input.json)"`.
39	
40	### Remove a node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID>
44	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> --output json
45	```
46	
47	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
48	- Removes the node from `nodes`
49	- Removes all connected edges
50	- Removes orphaned definitions (definitions no longer referenced by any node)
51	- Removes orphaned bindings (connector bindings are shared at the connector level — a binding is only orphaned when no remaining node uses that connector)
52	- Removes node variables from `variables.nodes`
53	
54	### List nodes
55	
56	```bash
57	uip maestro flow node list <ProjectName>.flow --output json
58	```
59	
60	Returns all nodes with their `id`, `type`, and `display.label`. Use this to discover node IDs before wiring edges or removing nodes.
61	
62	### Add an edge
63	
64	```bash
65	uip maestro flow edge add <ProjectName>.flow <SOURCE_NODE_ID> <TARGET_NODE_ID> --output json \
66	  --source-port <PORT> \
67	  --target-port <PORT>
68	```
69	
70	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
71	- Inserts edge into `edges` array with a generated `id`
72	- Sets `targetPort` (required — validate rejects edges without it)
73	
74	See each plugin's `planning.md` or [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md) for port names by node type.
75	
76	### Remove an edge
77	
78	```bash
79	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID>
80	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID> --output json
81	```
82	
83	### List edges
84	
85	```bash
86	uip maestro flow edge list <ProjectName>.flow --output json
87	```
88	
89	Returns all edges with `id`, `sourceNodeId`, `sourcePort`, `targetNodeId`, `targetPort`.
90	
91	### Configure a connector node
92	
93	After adding a connector node with `node add`, configure it with connection details:
94	
95	```bash
96	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
97	  --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>'
98	```
99	
100	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
101	- Populates `inputs.detail` (connectionId, method, endpoint, bodyParameters, etc.)
102	- Creates connection binding entries in `bindings_v2.json`
103	- Creates connection resource files under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
104	
105	The `--detail` JSON schema differs between connector activity nodes, connector trigger nodes, and managed HTTP nodes — see [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), and [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the exact fields.
106	
107	**Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file:
108	
109	```bash
110	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json
111	```
112	
113	### Configure a managed HTTP node
114	
115	After adding a `core.action.http.v2` node, configure it with target connector and connection details:
116	
117	```bash
118	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
119	  --detail '{
120	    "authentication": "connector",
121	    "targetConnector": "<TARGET_CONNECTOR_KEY>",
122	    "connectionId": "<TARGET_CONNECTION_ID>",
123	    "folderKey": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
124	    "method": "GET",
125	    "path": "/api/endpoint",
126	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
127	  }'
128	```
129	
130	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
131	- Wraps your fields into the full `inputs.detail` structure (connector: `uipath-uipath-http`, bodyParameters, configuration)
132	- Generates `bindings_v2.json` with the target connector's connection
133	- Creates a connection resource file under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
134	
135	See [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the full configuration workflow and JSON structure.
136	
137	### Validate
138	
139	```bash
140	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
141	```
142	
143	Run **once** after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Carve-Out Composite Operations
148	
149	These combine primitives only for workflows that are themselves carve-outs. Do not use them for non-carve-out structural edits; use [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) instead.
150	
151	### Replace manual trigger with connector trigger
152	
153	1. Remove the manual trigger (also removes its edges and orphaned definition):
154	   ```bash
155	   uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow start --output json
156	   ```
157	2. Add the connector trigger node:
158	   ```bash
159	   uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE> \
160	     --label "<LABEL>" --position 200,144 --output json
161	   ```
162	3. Re-wire edge from the new trigger to the next node:
163	   ```bash
164	   uip maestro flow edge add <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> <NEXT_NODE_ID> \
165	     --source-port output --target-port input --output json
166	   ```
167	4. Configure the trigger with connection and event parameters:
168	   ```bash
169	   uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> --detail '<TRIGGER_DETAIL_JSON>'
170	   ```
171	
172	See [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md) for the full `--detail` schema.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## Operations Not Supported by CLI
177	
178	These operations require the `Edit` tool. Use the [Edit / Write strategy guide](editing-operations-json.md) for:
179	
180	1. **Any non-carve-out structural edit** — node/edge CRUD, scheduled triggers, HITL QuickForm nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, and graph rewiring
181	2. **Node input updates** — the CLI does not have a `node update` command; use `Edit` to preserve node IDs and `$vars.{nodeId}` references
182	3. **Workflow variables** — add/remove/update `variables.globals`
183	4. **Variable updates** — add/modify `variables.variableUpdates` entries
184	5. **Output mapping on End nodes** — add `outputs` object with `source` expressions
185	6. **Subflows** — create `subflows.{nodeId}` with nested nodes, edges, variables
186

It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. ```json 605 "outputs": { 606 "result": { 607 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 608 } 609 } 610 ``` 611 612 --- 613 614 ## Complete Example 615 616 A flow with input, state, and output success_criteria:
  # Inverted twin of the positive routing.yaml grep.
  # `shell=True` in coder_eval Sandbox.run_command means `!` works as a bash
  # negator: grep -q exits 0 on match → ! flips to 1 (FAIL); exits 1 on
  # no-match → ! flips to 0 (PASS).
  - type: run_command
    description: "No uipath.ixp.* node landed in any .flow file (negative IxP routing)"
    command: '! grep -rqE "\"type\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"uipath\.ixp" --include="*.flow" .'
    expected_exit_code: 0
    suite_thresholds: {mean: 0.85}
